title: What should I say?
scope: The subjunctive (बोलूँ, बोले, बोलो, बोलें; हूँ/हो/हों, लूँ, दूँ) for suggestions, mild commands and uncertainty, negated with न; कि clauses after wish, request, possibility and necessity (ज़रूरी है कि, संभव है कि, निवेदन है कि, से कहो कि) against the future for confident expectation; the subjunctive auxiliary (खा रहा हो, जानती हो); चाहना with a direct infinitive or कि + subjunctive, and “be fond of”; conditionals with अगर/यदि … तो, नहीं तो; the suffix -वाला after nouns, adverbs and oblique infinitives (दूधवाला, नीचेवाला, बोलनेवाला, आनेवाला, “about to”)

vocab.en: to want, wish, be fond of
(suffix) person or thing connected with; about to

lessons.title: मैं क्या बोलूँ ?
lessons.desc: The subjunctive: “may I, should I, shall we”

items.q: Fill the gap: “Shall I make tea for you?”
items.hi: मैं आपके लिए चाय ___ ?
items.say: मैं आपके लिए चाय बनाऊँ ?
items.en: Shall I[0] make[4] tea[3] for[2] you[1]?
wrong: बनाए
बनाए goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes -ū̃: बनाऊँ.
बनाऊँगा
बनाऊँगा is the future, “will I make?”, a plain question about what will happen. An offer, “shall I?”, uses the subjunctive.
items.why: The subjunctive is the future without -gā/-gī/-ge: मैं बोलूँ, तू, यह, वह बोले, तुम बोलो, हम, आप, ये, वे बोलें. Masculine and feminine forms are the same.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita may come this evening.”
items.hi: शायद सीता आज शाम को ___ ।
items.say: शायद सीता आज शाम को आए ।
items.en: Sita[1] {may come}[0+5] {this evening}[2+3+4].
wrong: आएँ
आएँ is plural. Sita, spoken of plainly, takes the singular: आए.
आऊँ
आऊँ goes with मैं.
items.why: शायद “perhaps” often takes the subjunctive: शायद सीता आए “Sita may come”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You should come at nine tomorrow morning.”
items.hi: आप लोग कल सुबह नौ बजे ___ ।
items.say: आप लोग कल सुबह नौ बजे आएँ ।
items.en: You[0+1] should come[6] {at nine}[4+5] {tomorrow morning}[2+3].
wrong: आए
आए is singular. आप always takes plural agreement: आएँ.
आओ
आओ goes with तुम. आप takes -ẽ.
items.why: The आप subjunctive is a polite suggestion or mild command.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who should I give this letter to?”
items.hi: मैं यह चिट्ठी किस को ___ ?
items.say: मैं यह चिट्ठी किस को दूँ ?
items.en: Who[3] should I[0] give[5] this[1] letter[2] to[4]?
wrong: देऊँ
Not a word: देना is irregular. Its future is दूँगा, so the subjunctive is दूँ.
दे
दे goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes दूँ.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना follow their futures: हूँ, हो, हों — लूँ, ले, लें — दूँ, दे, दें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “He may not be at home today.”
items.hi: शायद वह आज घर पर न ___ ।
items.say: शायद वह आज घर पर न हो ।
items.en: He[1] {may not be}[0+5+6] {at home}[3+4] today[2].
wrong: हों is plural. वह, spoken of plainly, takes हो.
हूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना follow their futures: हूँ, हो, हों — लूँ, ले, लें — दूँ, दे, दें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children should speak only Hindi in class.”
items.hi: बच्चे क्लास में हिन्दी ही ___ ।
items.say: बच्चे क्लास में हिन्दी ही बोलें ।
items.en: {The children}[0] {should speak}[5] only[4] Hindi[3] in[2] class[1].
wrong: बोले
बोले is singular. बच्चे is plural: बोलें.
बोलूँ
बोलूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: The subjunctive is the future without -gā/-gī/-ge: मैं बोलूँ, तू, यह, वह बोले, तुम बोलो, हम, आप, ये, वे बोलें. Masculine and feminine forms are the same.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Should I have tea or coffee?”
items.say: मैं चाय लूँ कि कॉफ़ी ?
items.en: Should I[0] have[2] tea[1] or[3] coffee[4]?
wrong: लेऊँ
Not a word: लेना is irregular. Its future is लूँगा, so the subjunctive is लूँ.
ले
ले goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes लूँ.
items.why: Between two choices कि can mean “or”: लूँ कि … “should I take … or …?”.

items.q: Make it a suggestion (“shall we …?”)
wrong: हम बाज़ार जाऊँ ?
जाऊँ goes with मैं. हम takes -ẽ: जाएँ.
हम बाज़ार जाए ?
जाए is singular. हम takes the plural: जाएँ.
items.why: Drop -ge from the future: जाएँगे → जाएँ.
items.hi: हम बाज़ार जाएँगे ।
items.say: हम बाज़ार जाएँ ?
items.en: Shall we[0] go[2] {to the market}[1]?

items.q: What is the subjunctive of देना with आप?
wrong: देएँ
Not a word: देना is irregular. देंगे → दें.
देंगे
देंगे is the future. Drop -ge for the subjunctive: दें.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना follow their futures: हूँ, हो, हों — लूँ, ले, लें — दूँ, दे, दें.

items.q: What is the subjunctive of होना with वे?
wrong: हो
हो goes with तू, यह, वह and तुम. वे takes हों.
होंगे
होंगे is the future, “will be” or “must be”. Drop -ge for the subjunctive: हों.
items.why: होना, लेना and देना follow their futures: हूँ, हो, हों — लूँ, ले, लें — दूँ, दे, दें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki should not tell anyone this.”
items.hi: पिंकी यह बात किसी से न ___ ।
items.say: पिंकी यह बात किसी से न कहे ।
items.en: Pinki[0] {should not}[5] tell[6] anyone[3+4] {this}[1+2].
wrong: कहें
कहें is plural. Pinki, spoken of plainly, takes the singular: कहे.
कहूँ
कहूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: The subjunctive is made negative with न — न कहे “should not tell”.

lessons.title: ज़रूरी है कि …
lessons.desc: कि clauses after wish, request, possibility

items.q: Fill the gap: “It's important that the children go to sleep early.”
items.hi: ज़रूरी है कि बच्चे जल्दी ___ ।
items.say: ज़रूरी है कि बच्चे जल्दी सोएँ ।
items.en: {It's}[1] important[0] that[2] {the children}[3] {go to sleep}[5] early[4].
wrong: सोए
सोए is singular. बच्चे is plural: सोएँ.
सोते
सोते is the imperfective participle. After ज़रूरी है कि the verb is subjunctive.
items.why: After expressions of wish, request, possibility or necessity (ज़रूरी है कि, संभव है कि, निवेदन है कि, … से कहो कि) the कि clause takes the subjunctive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “It's possible that it may rain tonight.”
items.hi: संभव है कि आज रात को पानी ___ ।
items.say: संभव है कि आज रात को पानी पड़े ।
items.en: {It's}[1] possible[0] that[2] {it may rain}[6+7] tonight[3+4+5].
wrong: पड़ें
पड़ें is plural. In पानी पड़ना “to rain” the subject पानी is singular.
पड़ूँ
पड़ूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: After expressions of wish, request, possibility or necessity (ज़रूरी है कि, संभव है कि, निवेदन है कि, … से कहो कि) the कि clause takes the subjunctive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My request to you is that you do not smoke here.”
items.hi: मेरा आप से निवेदन है कि आप यहाँ सिग्रेट न ___ ।
items.say: मेरा आप से निवेदन है कि आप यहाँ सिग्रेट न पिएँ ।
items.en: My[0] request[3] {to you}[1+2] is[4] that[5] you[6] {do not smoke}[8+9+10] here[7].
wrong: पिए
पिए is singular. आप takes the plural: पिएँ.
पियो
पियो is the तुम form. आप takes -ẽ.
items.why: निवेदन है कि “the request is that …” is a polite formula followed by the subjunctive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “It is impossible that Mohan would lie.”
items.hi: यह असंभव है कि मोहन झूठ ___ ।
items.say: यह असंभव है कि मोहन झूठ बोले ।
items.en: It[0] is[2] impossible[1] that[3] Mohan[4] {would lie}[5+6].
wrong: बोलें
बोलें is plural. Mohan, spoken of plainly, takes the singular: बोले.
बोलो
बोलो goes with तुम.
items.why: संभव and असंभव है कि take the subjunctive: “it is (im)possible that he might …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am quite sure that Raj will come tomorrow.”
items.hi: मुझे पूरा यक़ीन है कि राज कल ___ ।
items.say: मुझे पूरा यक़ीन है कि राज कल आएगा ।
items.en: I[0] am[3] quite[1] sure[2] that[4] Raj[5] {will come}[7] tomorrow[6].
wrong: आए
आए is the subjunctive, for something uncertain or wished for. यक़ीन “confidence” calls for the future: आएगा.
आएगी
आएगी is feminine. Raj is a man.
items.why: A confident expectation (यक़ीन, विश्वास) takes the future, not the subjunctive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please tell Mohan that he should phone me.”
items.hi: मोहन से कहिए कि वह मुझे फ़ोन ___ ।
items.say: मोहन से कहिए कि वह मुझे फ़ोन करे ।
items.en: Please tell[2] Mohan[0+1] that[3] he[4] {should phone}[6+7] me[5].
wrong: करो
करो goes with तुम. The subject of the कि clause is वह — करे.
करें
करें is plural. वह, spoken of plainly, takes the singular: करे.
items.why: Reported commands: X से कहो कि … + subjunctive “tell X to …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “It isn't proper that you go out alone so late at night. (to a woman)”
items.hi: उचित नहीं है कि तुम इतनी रात को अकेली बाहर ___ ।
items.say: उचित नहीं है कि तुम इतनी रात को अकेली बाहर जाओ ।
items.en: It {isn't}[1+2] proper[0] that[3] you[4] {go out}[9+10] alone[8] {so late at night}[5+6+7]. (to a woman)
wrong: जाए
जाए goes with तू, यह and वह. तुम takes जाओ.
जाऊँ
जाऊँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: उचित है कि “it is proper that” takes the subjunctive. The तुम subjunctive looks like the command form: जाओ.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Don't phone Mohan now; he may be having his meal.”
items.hi: मोहन को अभी फ़ोन मत करो, शायद वह खाना खा रहा ___ ।
items.say: मोहन को अभी फ़ोन मत करो, शायद वह खाना खा रहा हो ।
items.en: {Don't}[4] phone[3+5] Mohan[0+1] now[2]; he[7] {may be}[6+11] {having his meal}[8+9+10].
wrong: हों is plural. वह, spoken of plainly, takes हो.
हूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: The subjunctive हो, हों as an auxiliary gives “may be …ing”, “may …”: खा रहा हो, जानती हो. The future होगा is surer: “must be”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Perhaps that American girl knows Hindi too.”
items.hi: शायद वह अमरीकन लड़की भी हिन्दी ___ हो ।
items.say: शायद वह अमरीकन लड़की भी हिन्दी जानती हो ।
items.en: Perhaps[0] that[1] American[2] girl[3] knows[6+7] Hindi[5] too[4].
wrong: जानता
जानता is masculine. लड़की is feminine.
जानते
जानते is masculine plural. लड़की is feminine singular.
items.why: The imperfective participle + हो — “may know, may be in the habit of”.

items.q: Make it less certain (“may be …ing”)
items.a: राज दफ़्तर में काम कर रहा हो ।
wrong: राज दफ़्तर में काम कर रहा है ।
है states a fact: “Raj is working”. “May be working” needs the subjunctive हो.
राज दफ़्तर में काम कर रहे हो ।
रहे is plural. Raj, spoken of plainly, takes रहा.
items.why: होगा “must be” becomes हो “may be”; रहा stays.
items.hi: राज दफ़्तर में काम कर रहा होगा ।
items.say: राज दफ़्तर में काम कर रहा हो ।
items.en: Raj[0] {may be working}[3+4+5+6] in[2] the office[1].

items.q: Fill the gap: “If Father is resting, we will come later.”
items.hi: अगर पिता जी आराम कर रहे ___ तो हम बाद में आएँगे ।
items.say: अगर पिता जी आराम कर रहे हों तो हम बाद में आएँगे ।
items.en: If[0] Father[1] {is resting}[3+4+5+6], we[8] {will come}[11] later[9+10].
wrong: हो
हो is singular. पिता जी takes the plural of respect: हों.
हूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: The continuous may stand in an अगर clause, with the subjunctive auxiliary.

items.q: Which means “Perhaps the guests are coming now”?
items.a: शायद मेहमान अभी आ रहे हों ।
wrong: शायद मेहमान अभी आ रहे थे ।
थे is past: “perhaps the guests were coming”.
शायद मेहमान अभी आ रही हों ।
रही is feminine. मेहमान is masculine: आ रहे हों.
items.why: The subjunctive हो, हों as an auxiliary gives “may be …ing”, “may …”: खा रहा हो, जानती हो. The future होगा is surer: “must be”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Suhas wants to go to London next year.”
items.hi: सुहास अगले साल लंदन ___ चाहता है ।
items.say: सुहास अगले साल लंदन जाना चाहता है ।
items.en: Suhas[0] wants[5+6] {to go}[4] to London[3] {next year}[1+2].
wrong: जाने
चाहना takes the direct infinitive: जाना चाहता है.
जाए
The subjunctive needs कि and a different person: चाहता है कि वह जाए. Here Suhas himself will go.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).

items.q: Fill the gap: “I want to ask you something. (a woman speaking)”
items.hi: मैं आप से कुछ पूछना ___ हूँ ।
items.say: मैं आप से कुछ पूछना चाहती हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] want[5+6] {to ask}[4] you[1+2] something[3]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: चाहता
चाहता is masculine. The speaker is a woman.
चाहिए
चाहिए is a separate construction with को (मुझे … चाहिए). With मैं as subject the verb is चाहना.
items.why: चाहना is a regular verb: चाहता, चाहती, चाहते + है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita wants me to read her letter.”
items.hi: सीता चाहती है कि मैं उसकी चिट्ठी ___ ।
items.say: सीता चाहती है कि मैं उसकी चिट्ठी पढ़ूँ ।
items.en: Sita[0] wants[1+2] me[4] {to read}[7] her[5] letter[6].
wrong: पढ़ना
Sita wants someone else to read, so the infinitive will not do. Use कि + subjunctive: कि मैं पढ़ूँ.
पढ़े
पढ़े goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes पढ़ूँ.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).

items.q: Fill the gap: “We want you to have a meal with us.”
items.hi: हम चाहते हैं कि आप हमारे साथ खाना ___ ।
items.say: हम चाहते हैं कि आप हमारे साथ खाना खाएँ ।
items.en: We[0] want[1+2] you[4] {to have}[8] a meal[7] with[6] us[5].
wrong: खाइए
खाइए is a command. After चाहना कि the verb is subjunctive: खाएँ.
खाए
खाए is singular. आप takes the plural: खाएँ.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan wanted us to come to his house.”
items.hi: मोहन चाहता था कि हम उसके घर ___ ।
items.say: मोहन चाहता था कि हम उसके घर आएँ ।
items.en: Mohan[0] wanted[1+2] us[4] {to come}[7] to his[5] house[6].
wrong: आएँगे
आएँगे is the future. After चाहना कि the verb is subjunctive: आएँ.
आओ
आओ goes with तुम. हम takes आएँ.
items.why: The subjunctive stays the same after a past चाहता था.

items.q: Which means “I want to go home”? (a man speaking)
wrong: मुझे घर जाना चाहता है ।
चाहना takes a direct subject, मैं. मुझे … goes with चाहिए, a separate construction.
मैं घर जाने चाहता हूँ ।
चाहना takes the direct infinitive, जाना, not the oblique.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).

items.q: Change it to “Mother wants you to …”
items.a: माँ चाहती हैं कि आप कल फिर आएँ ।
wrong: माँ चाहती हैं कि आप कल फिर आइए ।
आइए is a command and cannot follow चाहना कि. Use the subjunctive: आएँ.
माँ चाहती हैं कि आप कल फिर आएँगे ।
आएँगे is the future. After चाहना कि the verb is subjunctive: आएँ.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).
items.hi: आप कल फिर आइए ।
items.say: माँ चाहती हैं कि आप कल फिर आएँ ।
items.en: Mother[0] wants[1+2] you[4] {to come}[7] again[6] tomorrow[5].

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj wants his sisters to help him.”
items.hi: राज चाहता है कि उसकी बहिनें उसकी मदद ___ ।
items.say: राज चाहता है कि उसकी बहिनें उसकी मदद करें ।
items.en: Raj[0] wants[1+2] his[4] sisters[5] {to help}[7+8] him[6].
wrong: करे
करे is singular. बहिनें is plural: करें.
करना
Raj wants others to act, so use कि + subjunctive, not the infinitive.
items.why: मदद करना “to help”: X की मदद करना “to help X”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you have time, then help me.”
items.hi: अगर तुम्हारे पास वक़्त हो ___ मेरी मदद करो ।
items.say: अगर तुम्हारे पास वक़्त हो तो मेरी मदद करो ।
items.en: If[0] you[1+2] have[4] time[3], {then}[5] help[7+8] me[6].
wrong: कि
कि introduces a “that” clause. The “then” clause of a condition starts with तो.
और
और is “and”. A condition needs तो.
items.why: अगर (or यदि) … तो — the अगर clause may be imperfective, future or subjunctive; the तो clause is usually future or a command. अगर can be dropped, तो cannot.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you come in the evening, then we will eat together.”
items.hi: अगर आप लोग शाम को ___ तो हम साथ खाना खाएँगे ।
items.say: अगर आप लोग शाम को आएँ तो हम साथ खाना खाएँगे ।
items.en: If[0] you[1+2] come[5] {in the evening}[3+4], {then}[6] we[7] {will eat}[9+10] together[8].
wrong: आओ
आओ goes with तुम. आप लोग takes -ẽ: आएँ.
आऊँ
आऊँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: अगर (or यदि) … तो — the अगर clause may be imperfective, future or subjunctive; the तो clause is usually future or a command. अगर can be dropped, तो cannot.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If the shop is shut, then I will come back tomorrow. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: अगर दुकान बंद हो तो मैं कल वापस ___ ।
items.say: अगर दुकान बंद हो तो मैं कल वापस आऊँगा ।
items.en: If[0] the shop[1] {is shut}[2+3], {then}[4] I[5] {will come back}[7+8] tomorrow[6]. (a man speaking)
wrong: आऊँगी
आऊँगी is feminine. The speaker is a man.
आएगा
आएगा goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes आऊँगा.
items.why: The तो clause usually has the future: “I will come back”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you have any trouble, please tell me.”
items.hi: ___ आप को कोई तकलीफ़ हो तो मुझे बताइए ।
items.say: अगर आप को कोई तकलीफ़ हो तो मुझे बताइए ।
items.en: If[0] you[1+2] have[5] any[3] trouble[4], {please tell}[8] me[7].
wrong: कि
कि introduces a “that” clause. “If” is अगर.
तो
तो begins the second clause, “then”. The first clause begins with अगर.
items.why: अगर (or यदि) … तो — the अगर clause may be imperfective, future or subjunctive; the तो clause is usually future or a command. अगर can be dropped, तो cannot.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you are going to the market, then bring some fruit for me.”
items.hi: अगर तुम बाज़ार जा रहे हो तो मेरे लिए फल ___ ।
items.say: अगर तुम बाज़ार जा रहे हो तो मेरे लिए फल लाओ ।
items.en: If[0] you[1] {are going}[3+4+5] to the market[2], {then}[6] bring[10] some fruit[9] for[8] me[7].
wrong: लाऊँ
लाऊँ goes only with मैं.
लाता
लाता is the imperfective participle. The तो clause here is a command: लाओ.
items.why: The तो clause can be a command, and the अगर clause can be continuous.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If you don't get a bus, then come by auto.”
items.hi: अगर तुम्हें बस न ___ तो आटो से आओ ।
items.say: अगर तुम्हें बस न मिले तो आटो से आओ ।
items.en: If[0] you[1] {don't get}[3+4] a bus[2], {then}[5] come[8] by[7] auto[6].
wrong: मिलो
The subject of मिलना here is बस, the thing that is found, not तुम — मिले.
मिलें
मिलें is plural. बस is singular.
items.why: With मिलना “to be found, got”, the thing got is the subject and the person takes को.

items.q: Which conditional is grammatical?
items.a: पिंकी घर पर हो तो उसे यह किताब दो ।
wrong: अगर पिंकी घर पर हो उसे यह किताब दो ।
तो cannot be dropped. Only अगर is optional.
अगर पिंकी घर पर हो कि उसे यह किताब दो ।
The second clause begins with तो, not कि.
items.why: अगर (or यदि) … तो — the अगर clause may be imperfective, future or subjunctive; the तो clause is usually future or a command. अगर can be dropped, तो cannot.
items.say: पिंकी घर पर हो तो उसे यह किताब दो ।
items.en: {If Pinki is}[0+3] {at home}[1+2], {then}[4] give[8] her[5] this[6] book[7].

items.q: Fill the gap: “Hurry, otherwise we will be late.”
items.hi: जल्दी चलो, ___ तो हमें देर होगी ।
items.say: जल्दी चलो, नहीं तो हमें देर होगी ।
items.en: Hurry[0+1], otherwise[2+3] we[4] {will be late}[5+6].
wrong: अगर
अगर तो is not a phrase. “Otherwise” is नहीं तो.
भी
भी तो is not “otherwise”. “Otherwise” is नहीं तो.
items.why: नहीं तो “otherwise, if not”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Our milkman comes every morning at six.”
items.hi: हमारा ___ हर सुबह छह बजे आता है ।
items.say: हमारा दूधवाला हर सुबह छह बजे आता है ।
items.en: Our[0] milkman[1] comes[6+7] {every morning}[2+3] {at six}[4+5].
wrong: दूधवाली
दूधवाली is feminine, a milkwoman. आता is masculine.
दूधवाले
दूधवाले is plural or oblique. हमारा and आता are masculine singular.
items.why: वाला, वाली, वाले agree like an -ā adjective. It relates a person or thing to the noun, adverb or oblique infinitive before it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Ask the rickshaw driver how far the station is. (the driver is a man)”
items.hi: ___ से पूछो कि स्टेशन कितनी दूर है ।
items.say: रिक्शेवाले से पूछो कि स्टेशन कितनी दूर है ।
items.en: Ask[2] the rickshaw driver[0+1] how[5] far[6] the station[4] is[7]. (the driver is a man)
wrong: रिक्शेवाला
Before से the word is oblique: रिक्शेवाले से.
रिक्शेवाली
रिक्शेवाली is feminine. The driver here is a man.
items.why: The noun before वाला may itself be oblique: रिक्शा → रिक्शेवाला. Before a postposition, वाला becomes वाले.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who lives in the downstairs room?”
items.hi: ___ कमरे में कौन रहता है ?
items.say: नीचेवाले कमरे में कौन रहता है ?
items.en: Who[3] lives[4+5] in[2] the downstairs[0] room[1]?
wrong: नीचेवाला
Before में the phrase is oblique: नीचेवाले कमरे में.
नीचेवाली
नीचेवाली is feminine. कमरा is masculine.
items.why: After an adverb, वाला makes an adjective: नीचेवाला कमरा “the downstairs room”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are many Hindi speakers in London too.”
items.hi: लंदन में भी बहुत-से हिन्दी ___ हैं ।
items.say: लंदन में भी बहुत-से हिन्दी बोलनेवाले हैं ।
items.en: {There are}[6] many[3] Hindi[4] speakers[5] in[1] London[0] too[2].
wrong: बोलनावाले
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, बोलने.
बोलनेवाला
बोलनेवाला is singular. बहुत-से and हैं need the plural: बोलनेवाले.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + वाला names the doer: हिन्दी बोलनेवाला “Hindi speaker”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Hurry, the train is about to leave.”
items.hi: जल्दी करो, रेलगाड़ी ___ है ।
items.say: जल्दी करो, रेलगाड़ी चलनेवाली है ।
items.en: Hurry[0+1], the train[2] {is about to leave}[3+4].
wrong: चलनेवाला
चलनेवाला is masculine. रेलगाड़ी is feminine.
चलनावाली
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, चलने.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + वाला + है — “is about to …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children were about to eat.”
items.hi: बच्चे खाना ___ थे ।
items.say: बच्चे खाना खानेवाले थे ।
items.en: {The children}[0] {were about to eat}[1+2+3].
wrong: खानेवाली
खानेवाली is feminine. बच्चे is masculine plural.
खानेवाला
खानेवाला is singular. बच्चे is plural: खानेवाले थे.
items.why: With था, थी, थे — “was about to …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “In the coming month we will go to Mussoorie.”
items.hi: ___ महीने में हम मसूरी जाएँगे ।
items.say: आनेवाले महीने में हम मसूरी जाएँगे ।
items.en: {In}[2] the coming[0] month[1] we[3] {will go}[5] to Mussoorie[4].
wrong: आनेवाला
Before में the phrase is oblique: आनेवाले महीने में.
आनावाले
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, आने.
items.why: आनेवाला “coming, next” is an adjective made with वाला.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita is from Banaras.”
items.hi: सीता बनारस की ___ है ।
items.say: सीता बनारस की रहनेवाली है ।
items.en: Sita[0] is[4] from[2+3] Banaras[1].
wrong: रहनेवाला
रहनेवाला is masculine. Sita is a woman.
रहनावाली
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, रहने.
items.why: X का रहनेवाला “a resident of X, from X”; का agrees with रहनेवाला.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is the girl who sings?”
items.hi: गाना ___ लड़की कौन है ?
items.say: गाना गानेवाली लड़की कौन है ?
items.en: Who[3] is[4] the girl[2] {who sings}[0+1]?
wrong: गानेवाला
गानेवाला is masculine. लड़की is feminine.
गानेवाले
गानेवाले is plural or oblique. लड़की is singular and direct here: गानेवाली.
items.why: वाला, वाली, वाले agree like an -ā adjective. It relates a person or thing to the noun, adverb or oblique infinitive before it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki was just about to start her (own) work.”
items.hi: पिंकी अभी अपना काम शुरू ___ थी ।
items.say: पिंकी अभी अपना काम शुरू करनेवाली थी ।
items.en: Pinki[0] {was just about to start}[1+4+5+6] {her (own)}[2] work[3].
wrong: करनावाला
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, करने. And Pinki is a woman: करनेवाली.
करनेवाला
करनेवाला is masculine. Pinki is a woman.
items.why: With था, थी, थे — “was about to …”. Before वाला the infinitive is oblique, in -ne: बोलनेवाला, आनेवाला.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My work is about to finish.”
items.hi: मेरा काम ख़त्म ___ है ।
items.say: मेरा काम ख़त्म होनेवाला है ।
items.en: My[0] work[1] {is about to finish}[2+3+4].
wrong: होनावाली
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, होने.
होनेवाली
होनेवाली is feminine. काम is masculine.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + वाला + है — “is about to …”.

items.q: Which means “the woman from Delhi”?
wrong: दिल्लीवाला
दिल्लीवाला is masculine, “the man from Delhi”.
दिल्लीवाले
दिल्लीवाले is plural or oblique: “people from Delhi”.
items.why: वाला, वाली, वाले agree like an -ā adjective. It relates a person or thing to the noun, adverb or oblique infinitive before it.

items.en: Shall I[0] bring[2] water[1]?
wrong: लाए
लाए goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes लाऊँ.
लाओ
लाओ goes with तुम. मैं takes लाऊँ.

items.en: We[0] want[3+4] {to go}[2] to Agra[1].
wrong: जाने
चाहना takes the direct infinitive: जाना.
चाहिए
चाहिए is a separate construction with को. With हम as subject the verb is चाहना.

items.en: Pinki[0] wants[1+2] me[4] {to write}[7] her[5] a letter[6].
wrong: लिखना
Pinki wants someone else to write: use कि + subjunctive, लिखूँ.
लिखे
लिखे goes with तू, यह and वह. मैं takes लिखूँ.

items.en: If[0] Raj[1] comes[2], {then}[3] tell[5] me[4]. (to तुम)
wrong: कि
The second clause of a condition begins with तो, not कि.
आएँ
आएँ is plural. Raj, spoken of plainly, takes आए.

items.en: You[0] {should phone}[2+3] tomorrow[1]. (to आप)
wrong: करे
करे is singular. आप takes करें.
करो
करो goes with तुम. आप takes करें.

items.en: {It's}[1] possible[0] that[2] Mohan[3] {won't come}[5+6] today[4].
wrong: नहीं
The subjunctive is made negative with न.
आएँ
आएँ is plural. Mohan, spoken of plainly, takes आए.

items.en: {The upstairs}[0] neighbour[1] is[4] very[2] lazy[3]. (a man)
wrong: ऊपरवाली
ऊपरवाली is feminine. पड़ोसी is masculine.
ऊपरवाले
ऊपरवाले is plural or oblique. With है the neighbour is one man: ऊपरवाला.

items.en: Our[0] guests[1] {are about to arrive}[2+3].
wrong: आनेवाला
आनेवाला is singular. The guests are plural: आनेवाले हैं.
आनावाले
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, आने.

items.en: Do you[1] know[6+7] the man[4+5] {who lives}[3] upstairs[2]?
wrong: रहनेवाला
Before को the phrase is oblique: रहनेवाले आदमी को.
रहता
रहता is the imperfective participle. “Who lives” before a noun is रहनेवाला.

items.en: If[0] you[1] wish[2], {then}[3] I[4] {will come}[7] with[6] you[5]. (a man speaking)
wrong: चाहे
चाहे is singular. आप takes चाहें.
चाहिए
चाहिए is “ought, need”, a separate construction. “If you wish” is अगर आप चाहें.

items.en: {It's}[0+2] essential[1] that[3] we[4] reach[8] the station[7] {on time}[5+6].
wrong: पहुँचेंगे
पहुँचेंगे is the future. After ज़रूरी है कि the verb is subjunctive: पहुँचें.
पहुँचना
After ज़रूरी है कि the verb is a full subjunctive, पहुँचें, not the infinitive.

items.en: You[0] {should take}[3] this[1] book[2]. (to आप)
wrong: लेएँ
Not a word: लेना is irregular. लेंगे → लें.
ले
ले is singular. आप takes लें.

items.en: Should we[0] go[3] by[2] rickshaw[1] or[4] by[6] auto[5]?
wrong: जाऊँ
जाऊँ goes only with मैं. हम takes जाएँ.
रिक्शा
Before से the noun is oblique: रिक्शे से.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: शायद प्रकाश को यह बात मालूम हो ।
wrong: Prakash must know about this.
“Must” would be the future: मालूम होगा. हो is “may”.
Prakash doesn't know about this.
Nothing here is negative. शायद … हो is “may”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम मेरे भाई से मिलो ।
items.a: I want you to meet my brother.
wrong: I want to meet your brother.
That would be मैं तुम्हारे भाई से मिलना चाहता हूँ. Here तुम is the one who will meet.
You want me to meet your brother.
मैं is the one who wants; तुम मिलो is the wish.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मोहन अपनी छोटी बहिन को बहुत चाहता है ।
items.a: Mohan is very fond of his little sister.
wrong: Mohan needs his little sister.
“Need” would be चाहिए. चाहना with a person as object means “to be fond of”.
His little sister is very fond of Mohan.
Mohan is the subject (चाहता है). को marks the one he is fond of.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: अगर मोहन वापस आए तो उसे मेरा पता दीजिए ।
items.a: If Mohan comes back, please give him my address.
wrong: If Mohan comes back, please ask him for my address.
“Ask” would be पूछना. दीजिए is “please give”.
Mohan has come back and given me his address.
अगर … तो is “if … then”, and दीजिए is a request.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: गाड़ी चलानेवाला आदमी मेरा भाई है ।
items.a: The man driving the car is my brother.
wrong: My brother is about to drive the car.
“About to” would be चलानेवाला है with भाई as subject. Here चलानेवाला describes आदमी.
My brother drives the car every day.
Nothing here says “every day”. गाड़ी चलानेवाला आदमी is “the man driving the car”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: प्रताप दिल्ली जानेवाला था ।
items.a: Pratap was about to go to Delhi.
wrong: Pratap used to go to Delhi.
That would be जाता था. जानेवाला था is “was about to go”.
Pratap was on his way to Delhi.
That would be जा रहा था, the continuous. जानेवाला था is “was about to go”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मुझे पता नहीं था कि उसका घर इतनी दूर है ।
items.a: I didn't know that his house was so far away.
wrong: I knew that his house was far away.
पता नहीं था is “didn't know”.
His house isn't far away, as far as I know.
नहीं goes with पता था — “I didn't know”. दूर “far” is not negated.

items.q: How is the subjunctive formed?
items.a: Take the future and drop -gā, -gī or -ge
wrong: Add -e to the infinitive
The infinitive is not the base. Start from the future: बोलेगा → बोले.
Add हो to the imperfective participle
बोलता हो is the subjunctive auxiliary, “may speak (habitually)”. The plain subjunctive is one word, बोले.
items.why: The subjunctive is the future without -gā/-gī/-ge: मैं बोलूँ, तू, यह, वह बोले, तुम बोलो, हम, आप, ये, वे बोलें. Masculine and feminine forms are the same.

items.q: Which subjunctive form looks the same as a command?
wrong: The आप form: बोलें is the same as बोलिए
बोलें and बोलिए are different forms, though both can be polite requests.
The मैं form: बोलूँ
There is no command for मैं. बोलूँ is “may I speak?”.
items.why: This is why the तुम subjunctive (तुम रहो) reads as a mild command.

items.q: How is a subjunctive made negative?
wrong: With मत
मत goes with commands. The subjunctive takes न.
With नहीं
नहीं is the usual negative of the other tenses. With the subjunctive the book uses न, although नहीं is also heard in speech.
items.why: The negative for subjunctives is न.

items.q: In an “if” sentence, which word can be left out?
wrong: तो (अगर must stay)
It is the other way round: तो is essential.
Neither अगर nor तो
अगर is often dropped: राज आए तो …
items.why: अगर (or यदि) … तो — the अगर clause may be imperfective, future or subjunctive; the तो clause is usually future or a command. अगर can be dropped, तो cannot.

items.q: In an अगर clause about the future, which verb form makes the condition seem least likely?
wrong: The future: अगर वह आएगा
The future suggests the speaker thinks it likely.
The imperfective: अगर वह आता है
The imperfective is a neutral forecast.
items.why: Imperfective is neutral, future is likely, subjunctive is less likely (“should he come”).

items.q: When does चाहना take a plain infinitive?
items.a: When the one who wants is the one who acts
wrong: When the wish is polite
Politeness has nothing to do with it. The test is whether the subject changes.
When the wish is in the past
चाहता था कि … takes the subjunctive too, when the subject changes.
items.why: चाहना + direct infinitive when the one who wants is the one who acts (मैं जाना चाहता हूँ), with a different person, चाहना कि + subjunctive (मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम जाओ).

items.q: Which word is a formal (Sanskrit) synonym of अगर?
wrong: मगर
मगर means “but”.
कि
कि means “that”, or “or” between choices.
items.why: यदि वह आए तो … = अगर वह आए तो …

items.q: Which form means “about to go”?
wrong: जानावाला
Not a word: before वाला the infinitive is oblique, जाने.
जाता
जाता is the imperfective participle, “goes, going”.
items.why: Before वाला the infinitive is oblique, in -ne: बोलनेवाला, आनेवाला.

items.q: What can जानेवाला है mean?
wrong: “used to go”
That would be जाता था.
“must be going”
That would be जा रहा होगा.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + वाला + होना — “about to …”. Before वाला the infinitive is oblique, in -ne: बोलनेवाला, आनेवाला.
